title: Prefix cache tombstone accumulation — cleanup runbook and long-term mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity-constrained deployment on 2026-03-09 we observed a progressive degradation of prefix cache hit rates and an increase in memory churn that did not correlate with request volume. Investigation determined a tombstone accumulation pattern in the prefix cache index: expired/evicted entries were being marked but not reclaimed in several codepaths, and a rare race between the eviction worker and incremental compaction left tombstones behind. This manifested as higher GC pressure, increased slab fragmentation, and intermittent evictions of hot keys under load.

Timeline: 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC - alerts for elevated memory usage and reduced QPS on model-serving pool. 2026-03-09 03:25 UTC - rollback of a recent batch-priority change reduced pressure briefly. 2026-03-09 04:00 UTC - root-cause triage found prefix cache tombstone counts growing by 30x vs baseline. 2026-03-09 06:00 UTC - emergency mitigation (increase compaction frequency + restart of affected allocators) restored steady state.

Root cause: A confluence of three factors: 1) incremental evictions created tombstone markers to preserve K/V delta semantics for concurrent reads, 2) the background compaction path has a safelist that avoided reclaiming entries touched within the last X seconds — that threshold was set conservatively and combined with a recently introduced prioritization change to the eviction worker to reduce tail latency, leaving many tombstones untouched, 3) a race where the eviction worker would mark tombstones after the compaction scan had passed but before the next compaction scheduled, producing persistent markers.

Impact: Customer-facing latencies increased for a subset of long-context requests, some Dedicated customers saw capacity throttling when cache-backed efficiency dropped. No data corruption or user-visible incorrect outputs were found.

Work performed so far: emergency compaction tuning + allocator restarts, added telemetry to count tombstones per-shard and track time-since-mark, and a test harness that reproduces tombstone accumulation under synthetic workload. We also created a Grafana dashboard (link below) showing tombstone growth, compaction runs, and eviction worker throughput.

References: Confluence postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RI/ENG-20816+Prefix+Cache+Tombstone+Postmortem, GitHub PR (emergency): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3278, Reproducer harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/prefixcache-repro

Long-term goal: eliminate tombstone accumulation, ensure compaction is both performant and safe under high churn, and add preventative testing and invariants to catch regressions early.

acceptance_criteria: Automated CI reproducer demonstrates tombstone accumulation and verifies fixes prevent buildup
Telemetry shows tombstone growth rate reduced to baseline under mixed churn workload in canary cluster
Compaction change does not increase p99 latency by >5% for standard workloads
Runbook created describing emergency steps (alerts, compaction toggle, allocator restart) and owners
Post-deploy monitoring for 7 days with no tombstone alerts in canary clusters
